recent.summary: epic-breakdown.md E6.1 and decisions.md §10 claimed each enforcing command reads a flag, and proficiency is enforced in equipment_resolver.rs; actual three of the eight rules had a refusal to relax (prerequisites, budget, slots) plus the Wizard Known-spell rule; weapon, armor, alignment and encumbrance refused nothing, so E6.1 built them

SD-39 epic-breakdown.md E6.2 row claimed FILES YOU OWN: OverrideTag.tsx, selection DTOs, the Feats/Gear/Spells tabs, EquipmentPanel.tsx, list_held_equipment row, spec.json; actual selected_feats is Vec<String> and EquipmentSelection has 102 literal sites, so the flag lives in ledger.json; character_ledger.rs, pf1_adapter.rs, character_custom.rs and the adapters' response literals must change; the row's own picker step needs run.mjs to pass a click index

E6.1-receipt claimed the weapon flag refuses a wear and a buy for a weapon outside the class's list; actual the Market sells weapons as 'X (Base)', which no lookup read: 23 of 186 CRB Market weapon rows refused for a Wizard, 22 of them Improvised Weapon rows and 1 Armor Spikes; 0 Greatsword, 0 Longsword

E6.1-receipt claimed An unknown never refuses; actual an Elf Wizard was refused a Longsword, a Dwarf a Battleaxe, a Cleric the deity's weapon, a Fighter the Mind Shield: the verdict reads classes and three feats, and no grant can name a shield of no stated kind

E6.1-receipt claimed a spell off the class list saves under the flag for every class; actual the backend does, but the Spells tab withholds Add Spell from a non-caster, so a Fighter with the flag on had no way to it
E6.2-receipt claimed every record admitted under an override carries a row; actual a worn custom item moved onto a taken slot under the flag got no row; only a record not worn before did

E6.1-code-comment claimed An unchanged list wears nothing new, so what the slot flag let on stays when the flag goes off; actual any other change to the worn list then refused: with the flag off a worn ring could not be taken off or added while the head held two
